bodyMarkdown:
## Time & Work: Pipes & Cisterns

Treat this exactly like Time & Work, with one twist: an **outlet** pipe (a leak, or a pipe that
empties the tank) has a **negative** rate.

$$\text{Rate} = \frac{1}{\text{time to complete alone}} \qquad \text{Combined rate} = \sum \text{individual rates}$$

$$\text{Time} = \frac{1}{\text{combined rate}}$$

Inlet pipes: positive rate (they fill). Outlet pipes/leaks: negative rate (they empty). Never
average two times directly — always combine through rates.

workedExamples.stemMarkdown: Pipe A can fill a tank in 6 hours, pipe B in 8 hours. If both pipes are opened together, how long will it take to fill the tank?
workedExamples.solutionMarkdown: Rate of A $= \dfrac{1}{6}$, rate of B $= \dfrac{1}{8}$. Combined rate $= \dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{8} = \dfrac{4}{24} + \dfrac{3}{24} = \dfrac{7}{24}$. Time $= \dfrac{24}{7} \approx 3.43$ hours.

workedExamples.stemMarkdown: Pipe A fills a tank in 5 hours. Pipe B can empty the full tank in 10 hours. If both are opened together, how long will it take to fill the tank?
workedExamples.solutionMarkdown: Rate of A (inlet) $= \dfrac{1}{5}$. Rate of B (outlet) $= -\dfrac{1}{10}$. Combined rate $= \dfrac{1}{5} - \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{2}{10} - \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{1}{10}$. Time $= 10$ hours.

workedExamples.stemMarkdown: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 12 and 15 hours respectively. Both are opened together, but after 4 hours pipe A is closed. How much longer will pipe B alone take to fill the remaining tank?
workedExamples.solutionMarkdown: Combined rate $= \dfrac{1}{12} + \dfrac{1}{15} = \dfrac{5}{60} + \dfrac{4}{60} = \dfrac{9}{60} = \dfrac{3}{20}$. In 4 hours: $4 \times \dfrac{3}{20} = \dfrac{3}{5}$ of the tank is filled, leaving $\dfrac{2}{5}$. B alone fills at $\dfrac{1}{15}$ per hour, so time $= \dfrac{2/5}{1/15} = \dfrac{2}{5} \times 15 = 6$ hours.

formulaCards.title: Combined rate
formulaCards.bodyMarkdown: $$\text{Combined rate} = \sum \text{individual rates}, \quad \text{Time} = \frac{1}{\text{combined rate}}$$ Outlet/leak rates are negative.
formulaCards.exampleMarkdown: Fill in 4h, leak empties in 12h: combined = 1/4 - 1/12 = 1/6 → fills in 6h.

commonTraps: An outlet pipe's rate is subtracted, never added.
Never average two fill times directly (e.g. (6+8)/2) — you must combine through rates.
When a pipe is closed partway through, compute work done so far, then solve the remaining fraction with only the pipe(s) still open.
